approach: Root cause: the producer is stopped at a wall-clock limit per run (`budget.producer_timeout_s`, passed to `agent_spec` at crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs:344, stored as `spec.timeout` at crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs:457, and enforced at crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs:592-616). Its brief never states that limit or how to pace against it. Add one `## Time budget` section to the producer brief. A new `deadline_s: u64` field on `ProducerInputs` (briefs.rs:356) feeds it. One accessor in producer.rs, `producer_deadline_s(jc)`, supplies the number to both the invocation (producer.rs:344) and the brief builder (run/mod.rs:1178), so the stated and the enforced value cannot drift. The section renders unconditionally, so a fresh job, a retry from a seed, an unseeded retry and a resume all carry it. It tells the producer that each run, the first and any send-back, has this many seconds. It also says to do the smallest complete change first, run the full test suite at most once after the change is complete, and keep the tree reportable at every step. Prompt files, athena.toml and defaults.toml are untouched. No check, hold or refusal is added. Tests: two in briefs.rs, one in run/tests.rs that compares the spec's timeout, the recorded `caps.timeout_s` and the stored `brief-producer.md`. A CHANGELOG entry names the cause. This revision answers the one finding: criterion 6 now has a named seam, a fixture, and a fails-without. Each behavior demonstration (2, 3, 6, 7) names its production entry point, its fixture and its seam status. Criterion 6 is split into three whole simple commands, because the earlier `&&` chain was not one.

decisions.choice: Carry the deadline as one new `ProducerInputs.deadline_s: u64`, filled in core from a single `producer_deadline_s(jc)` accessor that the invocation also uses.
decisions.reason: One source for the enforced and the stated value, so they cannot drift (criterion 3). The context crate depends only on data (system facts, Crate reach), so it cannot read the config; the number has to arrive as an input. The documented meaning of the key is a bare `pub producer_timeout_s: u64` in `Budget` (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs:405). Its meaning is fixed by its use: `Duration::from_secs(timeout_s)` in `agent_spec` (reading.rs:457), enforced as the run's deadline (claude.rs:592). That is exactly the per-run limit the brief must state. The live athena.toml value is 86400 (athena.toml:49-51, with the comment that stage limits are 24 hours). Only the producer key is read here; the reader and verifier keys are not touched.

rejected.why: The live athena.toml sets producer_timeout_s = 86400 (athena.toml:51), so a constant would be false today and false again at the next change. The request also asks for the configured value.

rejected.option: Read `budget.producer_timeout_s` separately in producer.rs and in mod.rs
rejected.why: Two reads of one key can drift. The shared accessor makes the criterion-3 test about one value.

decisions.choice: Put the text in the generated brief (`producer_brief_with_evidence`, briefs.rs:681), as a new section function beside `no_change_section` (briefs.rs:757) and `checks_before_verifier_section` (briefs.rs:884).
decisions.reason: The producer prompt set is at 1043 of 1200 tokens (docs/system-facts.md) and briefs sit outside the budget sets, so no budget line moves. The brief is stored verbatim as `brief-producer`, so the criterion-3 test can read it.

rejected.why: Out of scope. It moves the producer token budget and the `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` test.

decisions.choice: State the limit per run, not per job, and do not state the stall window.
decisions.reason: `spec` is rebuilt on every pass of the producer loop with the same timeout (producer.rs:329-346), so a send-back gets a fresh limit. The stall window is `stall_window(spec.timeout, min_stall_window)` (claude.rs:598), which has a driver-set floor. Stating it would need a second field that can drift, and pacing does not need it.

rejected.why: Adds a field and a drift risk for no pacing gain. The stall watchdog already exists (claude.rs:596-619).

decisions.choice: No refusal, hold or watchdog is added. The expected share of newly refused readings is 0%.
decisions.reason: The brief tells the stage what it lacked, and the request asks to prefer that over a rule. Resume of a timed-out job already exists (`timeout_seed`, `keep_unfinished_work`, producer.rs:388-398; tests.rs:6161). The stall stop already exists (claude.rs:596-619). `check_reading_size` (reading.rs:370) already refuses a reading whose forecast exceeds the deadline; it is not changed. No parser, stem list or reading check changes, so no refusal_corpus case is added or mapped.

rejected.option: Refuse an identical-scope retry after a deadline
rejected.why: A refusal rule. It is not needed to give the stage the information, and it is listed out of scope.

decisions.choice: Answer to the finding: criterion 6 is demonstrated through the three configured check commands (athena.toml:94-109) run separately on the final tree, with no double.
decisions.reason: A behavior criterion needs a named seam. The seam is the checks Athena itself runs (fmt, clippy, test), as whole simple commands. The fixture is the real final working tree. The seam exists today.

rejected.option: Chain the three commands with `&&` in one demonstration
rejected.why: The verifier may run only whole simple commands, and a chain is not one.

risks.mitigation: The brief states whatever is configured, so it is true today and stays true if the value is lowered. The CHANGELOG entry says the 1800 s in the failure class is the earlier value. The pacing text does not depend on the size of the number.

One has `retry_from = Some(seed())`. One has a resume seed (`progress_note: Some(..)`, `candidate: Some(..)`). One has `retry_findings = Some(..)` with no seed. It also asserts the section appears exactly once in each brief.

demonstrations.method: New test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs. Build `repo()` (tests.rs:288). Read its committed athena.toml, replace `producer_timeout_s = 86400` with `producer_timeout_s = 4321` (assert the replace changed the text), and commit it with `commit_file` (tests.rs:358). Run `ask` and `go` through `athena_with(&repo, &state, PASSES, plenty_of_space, script)` (tests.rs:191), where `script` wraps `base_script()` (tests.rs:224) and records, for `Role::Producer`, `spec.timeout.as_secs()` and `spec.user_prompt`, the way the evidence test does (tests.rs:858-903). The reader forecast has p50 = 30 s (tests.rs:245), under 4321, so `check_reading_size` does not refuse. After the job lands, load records with `Records::load(&athena.git, &athena.head().unwrap())`, as at tests.rs:951. Read `jobs[id].briefs["brief-producer"]` and the producer invocation's `caps.timeout_s` (written from `spec.timeout` at invocation.rs:212).
demonstrations.observes: The recorded `spec.timeout` is 4321. The invocation record's `caps.timeout_s` is 4321. The stored brief's Time budget section contains "4321 seconds", and the prompt the agent received is byte-equal to the stored brief. 4321 is neither the repository value (86400) nor a constant in the code, so a copy or a constant would show.
